definitions.explanation: Originally the crest on a battle flag; now mostly figurative — a goal or principle held up as the cause one acts under.

examples.japanese: {改革|かいかく}を{旗印|はたじるし}にする。
{自由|じゆう}を{旗印|はたじるし}に{立|た}ち{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: They rose up under the banner of freedom.

examples.japanese: その{政党|せいとう}は{格差|かくさ}の{是正|ぜせい}を{旗印|はたじるし}に{掲|かか}げている。
examples.english: The party holds up the correction of inequality as its banner.

notes:
Literally the emblem on a military flag. In modern use almost always figurative: a principle or goal raised as a unifying cause. Frequently the object of {掲|かか}げる (to hold up), or used in the pattern Xを{旗印|はたじるし}にする.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旗印|はたじるし}を{掲|かか}げる: to raise a banner; to champion a cause
- ...を{旗印|はたじるし}にする: to make ... one's rallying cause

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スローガン: slogan — a catchphrase; {旗印|はたじるし} is the cause itself, not just its wording
- {目標|もくひょう}: goal — a target to reach, without the 'rally others under it' nuance
